One-sentence verdict: Computer and Information Research Scientists are not doing "business coding"; they conduct basic computer and information science research as theorists, designers or inventors, and develop solutions to problems in the computer hardware and software field; O*NET defines the occupation as "conduct research into fundamental computer and information science as theorists, designers, or inventors; develop solutions to problems in the field of computer hardware and software," and its tasks rank "analyze problems to develop solutions involving computer hardware and software" and "apply theoretical expertise and innovation to create or apply new technology (such as adapting principles for applying computers to new uses)" as the top two; this page follows the exact occupational scope of O*NET-SOC 15-1221.00.

Signals for exploring further: you are willing to live with open problems and uncertainty over the long term, and you treat "conclusions must be reproducible by peers" as a basic requirement; O*NET work context shows 100% use email every day, 94% work indoors in an environmentally controlled setting every day, 69% have face-to-face discussions every day (31% more than once a week), 64% have telephone conversations every day, 62% have sustained contact with others, 54% sit continuously or almost continuously (45% more than half the time), 54% have a great deal of decision freedom (37% limited), 51% consider work with a work group or team extremely important (43% very important), 48% have a great deal of task autonomy (24% some autonomy), 42% work more than 40 hours per week (58% at 40 hours), 34% consider the consequences of error very serious (24% serious), 12% consider their decisions very important to colleagues or company results (46% important), 58% of the work is moderately automated (25% not at all automated), and 100% never come into contact with disease or infection or whole body vibration or climbing.

Conditions for pausing before heavy investment: you have not yet completed one full loop of "problem definition and literature review — mathematical modeling and algorithm or system design — implementation and experimentation — result verification and reproduction — writing and peer review," and you have not verified the mandatory requirements of your institution and funders for research ethics, data and code management, intellectual property and technology export; this occupation's preparation level is Job Zone Five (extensive preparation), and the page's education distribution is expressed in three tiers: respondents said "some positions require a bachelor's degree," "some positions require a doctorate" and "some positions require a master's degree" (the page uses these three tiers and gives no percentages); the occupation page marks this code as Bright Outlook, but this page does not infer individual hiring probability from that.

Education, on-the-job training, professional certifications, licenses and job authorization must be verified separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Five (extensive preparation), and the page's education distribution is expressed in three tiers: respondents said "some positions require a bachelor's degree," "some positions require a doctorate" and "some positions require a master's degree" (the page uses these three tiers and gives no percentages); the page also lists 16 national certifications (such as Certified Computer Scientist, Certified Function Point Practitioner／Specialist, Certified LabWindows/CVI Developer, Certified in Open Source Intelligence, among others), but a certification is not equal to a degree, an employer appointment, signing authority or research qualifications; research ethics review involving human participants, data and code management, and intellectual property and technology export must be confirmed item by item according to the applicable jurisdiction and institution and funder requirements; this page describes tasks and boundaries based on O*NET and public sources, and does not present education or certifications as statutory qualifications.

In one sentence: this is an occupation in which "whether the question is asked correctly, whether the method holds up to reproduction, and whether the results are written clearly" determines success more than programming skill; if you are willing to treat reproducibility and honest boundaries as a method rather than a procedural requirement, it is worth serious consideration.

Give the theoretical basis or existing empirical support for the method and explain how it differs from existing methods; state the reasons for the trade-offs in the design (performance, complexity, maintainability, cost).

Fix the environment and dependencies and random seeds and data version, and keep runnable code and configurations; record results in a reproducible way and explain the sources of deviation; carry out data and code management and sharing as the institution and funders require.

State the applicable scope and failure cases and uncertainty in papers and reports; report results that do not support the hypothesis truthfully; do not selectively present experiments or delete unfavorable results.

The six directions share some capabilities with this occupation: computing and data foundations, problem decomposition and modeling, engineering implementation and verification, and written and oral expression. The real difference lies in the objective and responsibility: the management direction aims at coordinating people and budget and projects; the systems analysis direction aims at transforming requirements into solutions and delivering them; the database architecture direction aims at data models and storage governance; the data science direction aims at data-driven modeling and business delivery; while this occupation centers on basic research and the study and verification of new principles and new technology, with papers and methods and reproducible results as its main output. When choosing, it is advisable to first validate with one deliverable exercise in "problem definition — method and experiment plan — results and limitations statement," rather than comparing titles first.

The comparison basis is the occupational definition and tasks and work activities and work context descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 15-1221.00 page, the related occupations and adjacent occupation codes listed on that page, the adjacent occupation slug list registered in this evidence route, and the public occupational materials for each adjacent occupation; the comparison is an editorial compilation and does not constitute ethical, legal, intellectual property or research evaluation conclusions.

The table below compares the positions and occupations adjacent to this occupation: computer and information systems managers, architectural and engineering managers, natural sciences managers, computer systems analysts, database architects and data scientists. The four columns each answer the same kind of question: what the direction does, where the key difference from this occupation lies, and what kind of person is better suited to choosing it.

Computer and information systems managers coordinate the people, budget, projects and compliance of the information technology department, aimed at the stable operation and delivery of business systems; this occupation centers on basic research and the creation and verification of new principles and new technology.
People willing to coordinate the IT department and project delivery suit that direction; people willing to do basic research and verify new methods suit this occupation.
Mainly department management and enterprise system delivery and operations records.
Computer and information systems managers

Architectural and engineering managers coordinate the schedule, budget, people and compliance of engineering projects; this occupation mainly produces research problems and methods in the computer and information field.
People willing to coordinate engineering projects and teams suit that direction; people willing to do theory and method research suit this occupation.
Mainly engineering project management and acceptance records.
Architectural and engineering managers

Natural sciences managers coordinate natural science teams and projects and their compliance; this occupation's research object is the principles and systems of computing and information, not natural science phenomena themselves.
People willing to coordinate natural science teams and projects suit that direction; people willing to study computing and information principles suit this occupation.
Mainly natural science project management and experimental platform records.
Natural sciences managers

Computer systems analysts mainly translate business requirements into system solutions and coordinate implementation; this occupation mainly proposes and verifies new theories or methods and technical solutions, and does not carry responsibility for business system delivery.
People willing to do requirements analysis and system solution coordination suit that direction; people willing to do principle and method innovation suit this occupation.
Mainly requirements and solutions and implementation coordination records.
Computer systems analysts

Database architects mainly design and govern databases and data models and storage solutions; this occupation addresses broader computer and information science research problems and may involve hardware and algorithms and systems.
People willing to do data model and storage and governance design suit that direction; people willing to do principle and method research suit this occupation.
Mainly data model and database design and governance records.
Database architects

Data scientists mainly deliver data-driven modeling and analysis, aimed at business or product conclusions; this occupation focuses more on the novelty and reproducibility of the method itself and may extend to hardware and systems and theory.
People willing to deliver business conclusions through data modeling suit that direction; people willing to study new methods and new principles suit this occupation.
Mainly data modeling and analysis methods and business delivery records.
Data scientists

Moving from this occupation to an adjacent direction usually requires filling in new competencies and qualifications: the department management direction requires people and budget and compliance management experience; the engineering project management direction requires engineering schedule and acceptance management experience; the natural sciences management direction requires project coordination experience in the natural sciences; the systems analysis direction requires requirements analysis and business modeling and implementation coordination experience; the database architecture direction requires engineering experience in data models and storage and governance; the data science direction requires data modeling and business delivery experience. Computing and modeling and verification abilities can transfer, but the objectives and responsibility boundaries of each direction must be rebuilt.

paragraphs: Boundary: the six risk cards below summarize this occupation's tasks and work context to explain "what you will encounter and how it can be controlled"; they do not state incidence rates or accident probabilities; the applicable scope of each measure must be confirmed separately under the applicable jurisdiction and institution and funder rules.

Direct answer: the risks this occupation most needs to judge in advance come from three places — an unclear problem definition or unsuitable method making the effort ineffective, experiments and code and data not being reproducible making conclusions untrustworthy, and academic integrity and data and intellectual property and export compliance issues; the drain of long-term uncertainty and failed experiments, unclear interdisciplinary collaboration and requirements, and disputes over authorship and disclosure will amplify these three types of risk.

Tasks and context come from the current O*NET15-1221.00; wages OEWS2025, employment BLS2025—2035; risk control is an editorial suggestion, and the scope of ethics application is explained by jurisdiction using the relevant Chinese documents and U.S. OHRP guidance, with specific IP and export items not verified.
Positions responsible for problem definition and method design

A mismatched problem or method may weaken the conclusion and project progress; the specific impact depends on the hypothesis, evaluation and actual records, and it is not guaranteed that long-term investment will necessarily fail.

Write the problem as a testable hypothesis and specify the evaluation metrics and baseline; before starting, verify the feasibility of the method with a small-scale experiment or theoretical analysis; when necessary, review with a supervisor or collaborator before expanding the investment.
Starting with a vague objective; not doing a baseline comparison; treating "good results" as a conclusion without a measurable definition.
Positions responsible for experimentation and implementation and reproduction
Insufficient records of versions or randomness may reduce reproducibility; fixing a seed does not guarantee full reproduction, and the environment and randomness limitations must be stated.

Fix the environment and dependencies and random seeds and data version and keep runnable code and configurations; manage data and code as the institution and funders require and provide reproduction notes; report the sources of deviation and uncertainty truthfully.
Only runnable on a personal computer; not recording data processing steps; changing the pipeline without explanation when results are unsatisfactory.
Positions responsible for writing and publication and disclosure

Improper citation, authorship or disclosure may involve research integrity and rights disputes; whether it constitutes academic misconduct, infringement or export violation requires specific rules and facts, and is not asserted wholesale.

Complete approval and disclosure as the institution and funders require before submission and public release, and verify citations and authorship; consult the compliance position first for technology or data that may be subject to export control; retain approval and disclosure records.

Using others' results as background without citation; listing as an author without confirming contribution; publicly disclosing partner data or technical details that may be controlled without approval.
Positions responsible for handling data involving humans and privacy

Failure to fulfil applicable ethics or data protection conditions may create risk; first judge the jurisdiction, activity, exemptions and institutional policy, and do not treat all human-related research as uniformly requiring review and consent.

Articles 2, 4, 9 and 15 of China's 2023 Measures for Ethical Review of Science and Technology (Trial) limit the review and risk responsibility for activities involving humans, animals or other higher ethical risk and for the applicable units; Articles 2, 9 and 12 of the 2026 Measures for Ethical Review and Services of Artificial Intelligence Science and Technology (Trial) set out the scope of application and committee or commissioned-service review for AI research and development with potential ethical risk within China. The U.S. OHRP Lesson2 distinguishes human-subjects research subject to the Common Rule, non-research, research not involving human subjects and exemptions, and some exemptions still require limited IRB review; institutional policies may impose additional conditions. It cannot be said that all projects involving humans or all computer projects uniformly require approval or consent. The specific conditions for data handling, informed consent, IP and export must be verified separately by matter, and de-identification does not automatically grant processing or sharing authority.

Editorial risk examples: conducting an activity requiring approval without completing the applicable review; disclosing identifiable participant materials without authority; de-identification does not automatically make sharing lawful either.
Positions responsible for team and project organization and outreach
Misunderstanding of partners and requirements may affect delivery and schedule; the specific consequences depend on project evidence, and no inevitable causation is asserted.

Write the objectives and interfaces and deliverables and acceptance criteria clearly in writing before starting; confirm requirement changes per procedure and update the plan; retain meeting and confirmation records.
Substituting oral consensus for written agreements; not documenting requirement changes; not defining partner data and interface authority clearly.
Positions responsible for coping with long-term uncertainty and failed experiments
Repeated failure may bring pressure; misconduct such as data manipulation is not inferred directly from failure or psychological pressure.

Treat failed experiments as information and record the reasons and boundaries of failure; use mentor and collaborator and psychological support resources per institutional policy; keep method and data decisions under pressure reviewable.
Hiding negative results; modifying data or the pipeline under pressure; enduring alone without seeking review and support.

entries.question: What do computer and information research scientists do every day?

entries.answer: Computer and information systems managers coordinate the people and budget and projects and compliance of the information technology department; architectural and engineering managers and natural sciences managers coordinate engineering and natural science teams respectively; computer systems analysts mainly translate business requirements into system solutions and coordinate them; database architects mainly design and govern databases and data models and storage solutions; data scientists mainly deliver data-driven modeling and analysis; this occupation centers on basic research and the study and verification of new principles and new technology, with papers and methods and reproducible results as its main output. Shared competencies do not mean interchangeability: the objectives and responsibility boundaries differ.
entries.question: Where is the boundary between this occupation and adjacent occupations?

entries.answer: It cannot be inferred that way. The core tasks of this occupation include problem definition and theoretical modeling, experimental and system implementation and reproduction verification, and academic judgment about conclusions and limitations; these steps rely on professional training and academic responsibility and institutional authorization. In addition, the ILO exposure index registered in this evidence route is only a task exposure measure, not a replacement rate or a forecast of job losses. The more reliable use of tools is drafts of literature and code and data and documents.
entries.question: Will AI replace computer and information research scientists?

entries.answer: From the task structure, the steps affected earlier are the structured and digitizable ones: literature search and summaries, code scaffolding and boilerplate and debugging assistance, data processing and charts and document drafts, and the generation of some experiment configurations. Affected later are the steps requiring judgment and responsibility: problem definition and hypothesis generation, experimental design and validity judgment, judgments about conclusions and limitations and uncertainty, and ethics and authorship and export review. It must be emphasized: this judgment is an editorial compilation, not an exposure measure or job forecast provided by the sources.

These abilities rely on professional training and academic responsibility; replacing any of these steps with tool output makes "who is accountable for research conclusions and academic integrity" unanswerable.

description.text: Computer and Information Research Scientists conduct basic computer and information science research as theorists, designers and inventors, centered on problem definition and theoretical modeling, system and tool implementation and experimentation, and team and research organization and output: the 15 tasks and work context, the U.S. wages and employment (per the route requirement this round does not transcribe static figures and provides only the query entry and scope), the handling of the mainland China module-level wage gap and the decision not to publish a figure, entry and ethics and data and disclosure paths, and the method and reproduction and compliance boundaries and the exercise are all laid out in one view.

subject.name: Computer and Information Research Scientists
subject.summary: Conduct basic computer and information science research as a theorist, designer or inventor, and develop solutions to problems in the computer hardware and software field: analyze problems to develop solutions involving computer hardware and software; apply theoretical expertise and innovation to create or apply new technology; conduct logical analysis of business and scientific and engineering and technical problems and build mathematical models for computer solution; evaluate project plans and proposals to determine feasibility; design computers and the software that runs on them; maintain network hardware and software and direct security measures and monitor availability; participate in interdisciplinary projects such as virtual reality and human-computer interaction or robotics; assign tasks and set goals and performance standards and evaluate work; direct the daily operations of a department and coordinate projects with other departments; participate in staffing decisions and supervise the training of subordinates; and approve, prepare, monitor and adjust operating budgets.
